rationale: YES needs Musk and Trump to give substantive backing to different candidates in the same 2026 US race. Research shows Musk's roughly $366M this cycle went to Trump-aligned Republican groups (SLF for Paxton, CLF, RGA). He sat out Massie's primary against Trump's pick, and his one listed endorsement (Ramaswamy) matches Trump's. Primaries are over and their relationship has thawed, so a split in the last two weeks is unlikely. There is some residual chance of an obscure race or ballot measure I missed.

Democrats lead all three races: NC Cooper by about 8.5 (Likely D), MN Flanagan by 3-4, ME Jackson by about 2.6 over Collins in averages. Collins beat her polls by a wide margin in 2020, and Maine is a near toss-up, while MN gives a smaller extra R chance. That puts the chance of at least one R win a little above even. A search snippet mentioned a market Senate-control figure; I ignored it.

YES needs Lula to win the October 25 runoff by less than 4 points of valid votes. Recent polls lean Flávio (Datafolha 51-49 valid votes; aggregate about 52-48; Quaest 46-44), with some polls showing Lula ahead. I put Lula's win chance near 35%, and most Lula wins would be narrow (under 4), giving about 25%. A search result showed Polymarket/Kalshi prices; I ignored them.

Kreiss-Tomkins leads every recent poll: ASR 54-46 after ranked-choice rounds, NYT/Siena 52-48, RCP average +7.4. Cook moved the race to Lean D on October 13, helped by a split Republican field. The case against is Alaska's Republican lean, a history of polls overstating Democrats there, and Cook's warning that the race will be closer than polls show.

Mid-October reporting says Mojtaba Khamenei has no verified public photo or video since taking office. The only exception is an undated, disputed August clip, and his October messages are text only. The status quo of no appearance has held for months and only about 13 days remain, so the chance is low, though state media could release footage at any time.

Yisrael Beytenu polls about 8-9 seats, far behind Eisenkot's Yashar (about 21-26), Likud (about 19-21) and Bennett (about 11-13). Lieberman becoming PM would need an extraordinary coalition deal, and there is no sign of one.

Trump won, so the question is live. A DOJ/DEA final order (effective April 28, 2026) moved FDA-approved and state-licensed medical marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III, a real federal rescheduling of marijuana under Trump. Full rescheduling of all marijuana is still pending (ALJ proceeding reportedly stayed September 29), so the result turns on whether the creator counts the partial action. I lean YES because the main ask, getting marijuana out of Schedule I, was partly met.

YES needs an in-person Russia-Ukraine meeting (direct, or indirect through mediators in person) on peace terms by October 31. The US proposed a technical-level trilateral by end of October, possibly in the UAE, and Kyiv agreed. But Ushakov said Ukrainian strikes 'thwarted' a quick resumption, no date is set, and Ukrainian sources expect no serious talks before spring. Earlier 2026 rounds (Abu Dhabi, Geneva) show quick scheduling is possible, so this is not near zero.

The Houthis seized Perim on about September 11, 2026, and I found no reporting of a counteroffensive taking it back. Saudi-Houthi fighting is escalating and Trump has floated US strikes, but the question needs control actually established on the island, not raids or bombardment, in under two weeks. Amphibious retakes rarely happen that fast.

The June MoU expired or collapsed. Talks now run only through Qatari and other intermediaries, are stuck on sequencing, and the US is reportedly weighing new strikes. A signed final deal with concrete, measurable nuclear limits in about six weeks is very unlikely, though election-timed announcements leave a small chance.

Polls lean slightly to Peltola: RCP average 48.8-47.4, DDHQ about +2.5, NYT/Siena +7, though some September polls had Sullivan ahead. Cook rates it a toss-up. As an incumbent in an R+10ish state where polls have often overstated Democrats, Sullivan stays competitive, so I put him a bit below even. A search result reported Polymarket/Kalshi prices; I ignored them.

Incumbent Hobbs leads Biggs in every recent poll: PollsMax average D+7.3 over 26 polls, Equis +6, HighGround about +17. Non-market models give about 69% on a narrower D+4 margin. Biggs is a weak general-election candidate, but Arizona is a swing state and the model gap tempers my number. A search result showed a Kalshi price; I ignored it.
